newsitem.title: CANADA: Gandalf shares drop, may seek protection.
newsitem.headline: Gandalf shares drop, may seek protection.

text.p: Gandalf Technologies Inc shares dropped on Wednesday after a statement late Monday that the beleaguered computer parts maker had exhausted existing credit lines and may be required to seek court protection from creditors.
As Gandalf resumed trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange after Tuesday's Canada Day holiday it dropped 0.22 to 0.87 in active trading. The share's 52-week in Toronto low is 0.70.
On Nasdaq Galdalf's shares slipped 1/8 to reach 5/8, still above their 52-week low of 16/32.
Gandalf, based in the Ottawa suburb of Nepean, said on Monday that its credit facilities has exceeded the amount authorized by the Royal Bank of Canada and it had received no formal buyout offers.

"In the absence of additional financing and if no purchaser is forthcoming the company may be required to seek court protection from its creditors in order to permit it to attempt to reorganize and restructure its affairs," it said.
Analyst Brian Piccioni at Marleau Lemire said Gandalf may be running out of time after months of financial problems. "It looks like we're getting pretty close to the end," he said.

Piccioni added that a tumbling stock price and company value could increase the company's attractiveness to potential buyers. In Toronto, Gandalf has fallen from a 52-week high of 11.20 and from 8-12/32 on Nasdaq.
"The irony is: yeah, a bad stock price could be good for the company's long-term existence," he said.
But an analyst who requested anonymity said that the stock price did not reflect the company's real value. "Potential buyers aren't restrained by the share price."
"I think the fact that they haven't had an offer yet for the company suggests that the sale of the company is not a very good option," he said.
Gandalf may have no choice but to seek creditor protection in the end, the analyst said. "There's one option that doesn't go away and that's it (creditor protection) as time moves forward."
Piccioni noted that Gandalf just ended its first quarter on June 30 and would release its results in the next few weeks, unveiling the amount of its red ink.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109 or lydia.zajc@reuters.com))
